text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The government decided to speed its investigation into the curcumstances surrounding the problems of Aurobank, Innovation and Litimpeks Bank. Litimpeks was reopened last summer six months after being shut by the authorities but Innovation is still being restructured while Aurobank has been shut.
- The RAND Institution's Ronald Asmus told the newspaper that the Baltic states were unlikely to be included in a first round of NATO expansion.
- The paper quoted Swedish press sources as saying that U.S. President Bill Clinton will visit Lithuania this summer.
- 30 people have called the government's new corruption hotline. Most complaints were against council officials, the police and the prosecutor's office.
- 40 kgs of mercury were discovered in glass bottles in a courtyard not far the centre of Vilnius. One of the bottles was broken and some of the poisonous material had spilt.
